title: The lab's biosphere page
question: Reading this cold, with no explanation from me: can you tell whether anything in the box is reproducing, and how far it has got? If a line is unreadable, name it.
context_md:
**What this is.** The evolution lab's Running phase asks you to watch evolution happen, and an ant is two dark cells at play zoom -- findable only because it moves, and a dead one has stopped moving. This page is the other half of that answer: numbers beside the box, opened with `Tab`.

**Same box, same run, two moments.** The left pane is 1,800 frames in, the right 27,000. Everything on the page is about the box on the left of the same picture.

**What I have already checked, so you don't have to.** Every number here has been put through a box whose answer was known first: an empty box reports zeroes and says so rather than drawing a headline of them; a plants-only bed reports plants *and* reports no animals; killing half the stand mid-run makes the strips fall. `ANT CANNOT BREED` is correct rather than broken -- the shipped ant cannot pay for a child, and the page says by how much.

**What I want your eye on is the reading, not the arithmetic.** Is it too dense? Does any row need a word it hasn't got? And is the right-hand side the right place for it, or should the page be on the left with the box on the right?

items.label: 1,800 frames in
items.caption: eight herbs planted, one ant colony, nothing has bred yet

items.label: 27,000 frames in
items.caption: the stand has bred three times over; the colony has lost two thirds of its ants and produced none
